partially_covered.missing: No explicit data properties for organization contact info, legal form, etc.
Item details (e.g., description, product code) not modeled as properties of Item
No explicit cardinality or mandatory fields for D96A directory; SHACLConstraint class is present but not detailed

cq_coverage.details: Most core questions about invoice structure, participants, roles, items, and amounts are covered. Some detail-level and validation-related CQs are only partially supported due to lack of fine-grained attributes and explicit SHACL constraints.

strengths: Rich class hierarchy reflecting EDIFACT structure
Comprehensive use of cardinality restrictions and functional properties
Disjointness axioms present for key classes
weaknesses: No general class axioms (GCAs) for complex definitions
No owl:equivalentClass axioms for necessary and sufficient conditions
Limited use of advanced constructs (e.g., allValuesFrom, someValuesFrom)

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4: Missing domain or range for some properties (none detected, but always verify)
P7: Missing inverse properties for some relations (not all relations need inverses, but coverage is good)
reasoner_risks: Hermit/Pellet may struggle if SHACL constraints are implemented as individuals rather than axioms
No non-standard datatypes detected, so datatype-related failures are unlikely

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Enrich the Organization and Item classes with additional data properties (e.g., organization legal name, VAT ID, item description, product code) to fully answer CQ5 and CQ8.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves coverage for information displayed about organizations and items sold.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Define explicit SHACL constraints as individuals or axioms for mandatory fields and logical consistency, especially for CQ13.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables automated validation and improves interoperability.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce general class axioms (GCAs) and owl:equivalentClass definitions for key classes (e.g., Invoice, OrganizationRoleAssignment) to strengthen semantic rigor.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Richer axiomatization and better support for reasoning.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand technical vocabulary and code mappings for EDIFACT segments and elements, including more segment types and element codes.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves coverage of EDIFACT-specific queries and supports integration.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add more advanced property characteristics (e.g., transitive, symmetric) where appropriate, and consider modeling temporal properties (e.g., validity periods for roles).
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enhances expressiveness and supports more complex queries.

summary: This ontology provides a robust foundation for modeling EDIFACT invoice messages and procurement scenarios, with strong coverage of core structure, roles, and amounts. Some detail-level and validation-related competency questions require further enrichment, particularly for organization and item attributes and explicit SHACL constraints. The ontology follows OWL 2 best practices and is reasoner-friendly, but would benefit from deeper axiomatization and expanded technical vocabulary.
